subtitle: Fort Bend County and Brookstone, LP · RFP 17-037 · $20,447,000 · The agreement and Exhibit A (proposal). The schedule of values, document listing, and wage determination are not shown, and the signature blocks in this copy are blank.

results.title: Payment Terms
results.body: Contractor submits monthly Applications for Payment on the AIA form for services performed through the 10th of each month (Section 3.3). Each needs a certification, a partial lien waiver for the prior application, and a payroll and bills affidavit, with unconditional waivers from all trades at final payment (Sections 3.3.1 to 3.3.3). County pays uncontested amounts within 30 days after receipt, so payment is not conditioned on any third party (Section 3.4). Retainage is 5%, described as released at final completion of the entire Project (Section 3.4), yet at substantial completion County advances the balance less 50% of retainage and reserves for punchlist and claims (Section 3.5). Final payment waits for acceptance, lien clearance, waivers, and the Certificate of Occupancy (Section 3.5), then a release (Section 3.6). Flag: the two retainage provisions conflict, and County may withhold for any default, including subcontractors' (Section 3.4).

results.title: Changes and Claims
results.body: Any change to the Services must be approved in advance and authorized by County (Section 3.2), and the agreement can be amended only in a writing signed by both parties (Section 6.1). Total payments cannot exceed the $20,447,000 maximum without an approved change order (Section 3.1). Allowance overruns and underruns adjust the price by change order, with a 6% markup on allowances (Ex. A.2, Ex. A.3). Pending change directives and unresolved change orders are capped at 1% of the original amount unless both parties agree otherwise (Ex. A.5). Not addressed in this contract: notice deadlines for claims, pricing methods for other changes, and a duty to keep working during disputes. Flag: Contractor has no payment right for work County has not authorized in advance (Section 3.2), and County alone decides how Owner Contingency is spent (Ex. A.4).

results.title: Schedule and Delay
results.body: Time runs from receipt of the Notice to Proceed and ends no later than 485 calendar days later, subject to extension by County (Section 5.1). Substantial completion after that date costs $250 per calendar day, deducted from final payment, with no cap stated (Section 5.2). Delays of seven or more consecutive days caused by intentional County or Architect acts, separate contractors, ordered changes, or other causes both parties agree were beyond Contractor's control earn an extension, for a reasonable time County determines (Section 7.6). Either party may still pursue delay damages, so no no-damages-for-delay clause appears (Section 7.6). Excess normal weather days earn time (Ex. A.II), and hurricane delays are force majeure with reimbursed extended general conditions (Ex. A.7). Milestones, a final completion deadline, schedule updates, and acceleration are not addressed in this contract. Flag: extensions need County's agreement, and County sets their length.

results.title: Risk Transfer
results.body: Contractor must indemnify and defend County against losses arising from Contractor's activities that result from its negligent acts or omissions (Section 12.1). The duty to defend is absolute, survives termination, and continues until a court finds Contractor's acts are not at issue (Sections 12.3, 12.4). Flag: the indemnity extends to a finding that County was negligent in selecting Contractor (Section 12.5). For insured claims, Contractor's liability is limited to insurance proceeds (Section 12.6). Required coverage is $1,000,000 per occurrence and $2,000,000 aggregate general liability, $1,000,000 auto and employers' liability, and workers' compensation, with County and Commissioners Court as additional insureds and waivers of subrogation (Sections 10.1, 10.2). Builder's risk covers 100% of the Contract Sum, plus a $10,000,000 existing-structure endorsement (Sections 10.4.1, 10.4.3.4). A 100% performance and payment bond is due within ten days of signing (Section 11). Trade contractors must also indemnify County (Section 12.7).

results.title: Termination and Disputes
results.body: County may terminate for convenience on 30 days' written notice (Section 7.1), or for cause if Contractor misses the performance time, or materially breaches and fails to cure within ten calendar days of notice (Section 7.2.1). A termination later found improper converts to convenience (Section 7.2.2). Contractor may terminate only if unable to perform for 30 consecutive days through no fault of its own (Section 7.3). On termination, County pays for services provided and unbilled, and no other fees follow (Sections 7.4, 7.5). The right to suspend work is not addressed in this contract, nor are notice steps, mediation, arbitration, or attorneys' fees for disputes. Texas law governs, venue is Fort Bend County, and County's sovereign immunity is not waived (Section 19). Both sides waive consequential damages, including on termination (Ex. A.8). Flag: the missed-deadline default has no cure period, and Contractor's only exit right is narrow.
